answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by metering entry the way a river is metered at its inlet. Each new identity must draw a measured share of a scarce verification resource, and every completed task returns a signed nectar of credit that reviewers outside its cluster countersign. Stakes grow after each failed audit, so a hundred clones need a hundred metered entries and a hundred countersignatures. Influence then follows audited history, not registration.
